label: SIMULATED
caveat: Simulated NECB 2020 archetype buildings (NRCan BTAP, CWEC 2020 typical weather), not real buildings or bills: costs at today's stored tariffs for comparison only.
method: Archetype costs (owner decisions 86-114): each simulated BTAP building is priced month by month over its simulated year with the utility tariffs stored today for the city named in its weather file, in the rate class its own simulated load qualifies for under each utility's published limits. Per-day and per-30-day charges use each month's actual days, blocks apply per month, demand charges use the month's highest 15-minute demand (kVA = kW / the usage levels' power factor) with each tariff's ratchet over a repeating simulated year, time-of-use and on-peak energy is split by the simulated hours in clock time, and taxes and rebates follow data/models/taxes.json. Market energy (Ontario market price plus Class B Global Adjustment, Alberta pool energy) is estimated from the building's own load shape and the observed market history, as in owner decision 12. A comparison at today's prices, not a forecast or a bill (decision 114).

Class: Toronto Hydro by the average of the 12 monthly highest 15-minute demands against each class's stored limits (apartment buildings of more than 6 units on a 50 kW and over class, decision 167); ENMAX Power by its own tests over the repeating simulated year (more than 150 kVA in two months: D310; 5,000 kWh in six months: D300; otherwise D200). Gas: Enbridge Rate 6 (apartments included, per Enbridge's own rate-class evidence); ATCO Gas Low or Mid Use by annual GJ.

Supply: in Toronto, Regulated Price Plan time-of-use prices where O. Reg. 95/05 makes the account eligible, otherwise the market price plus the Class B Global Adjustment; in Calgary, ENMAX Energy's Rate of Last Resort below 250,000 kWh a year, otherwise pool energy. Market energy is estimated from each building's own load shape and the observed market history of the latest 60 complete months (labelled estimated).

Ontario charges on energy, per-kWh transmission and per-kWh regulatory charges use loss-adjusted kWh (the record's published secondary-metered total loss factor), as the OEB bill calculator does; the representative models do not apply loss factors.

Clock time: time-of-use and on-peak periods read local clock time (an hour later inside daylight saving) with each tariff's holidays on the 2006 calendar; bills follow the simulation's standard-time months.

Taxes and rebates from data/models/taxes.json; the Ontario Electricity Rebate tests the average monthly peak (50 kW or less) or the annual use (250,000 kWh or less), and apartment buildings get it as residential complexes (decision 103).
not_applied: Retailer contracts, energy marketers and Class A Global Adjustment (decision 98).
Alberta retailer charges and margins above the pool price for sites using 250,000 kWh a year or more.
The City of Calgary Local Access Fee (no rate in ENMAX Power's schedule), as in the representative models.
Contract, interruptible and seasonal gas services (decision 4); Enbridge's Rider I expansion surcharges (conditional).
Primary-voltage service, customer-owned transformers and contract demand (decision 113).
Daylight saving in the simulated schedules: the buildings run an hour later on the clock in summer (decision 112).
